old: Living tissue contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen in higher proportion than the earth's crust. In the human body by weight, oxygen is about 65%, carbon 18.5%, hydrogen 9.5% and nitrogen 3.3%. Water is the most abundant compound in cells. Chemical analysis separates an acid-soluble pool of micromolecules (molecular weight below 1000 Da) from an acid-insoluble fraction. The acid-insoluble fraction contains proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and lipids. Lipids are not polymers but appear here because membranes break into insoluble vesicles. Proteins are heteropolymers of 20 amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Their structure has primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary levels. Polysaccharides are chains of monosaccharides joined by glycosidic bonds. Cellulose is a homopolymer of glucose; starch stores energy and gives a blue colour with iodine; inulin is a fructose polymer; chitin forms exoskeletons. Lipids include fatty acids, glycerides and phospholipids such as lecithin. Nucleic acids are polynucleotides linked by phosphodiester bonds. Watson–Crick B-DNA has 10 bp per turn and a pitch of 3.4 nm.

old: Anton von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell. Robert Brown later discovered the nucleus. In 1838 Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist, observed that all plants are made of different kinds of cells that form tissues. In 1839 Theodore Schwann, a British zoologist, studied animal cells. He reported that cells have a thin outer layer, now called the plasma membrane, and that the cell wall is unique to plant cells. Together, Schleiden and Schwann proposed the cell theory. It did not explain how new cells form. In 1855 Rudolf Virchow added that new cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula). Modern cell theory states two things. First, all living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells. Second, all cells arise from pre-existing cells. An organism made of one cell is unicellular, and one made of many cells is multicellular. Anything less than a complete cell cannot live independently.
